## Why

The ui role reported this as tool feedback (deterministic-check) on ork in ork run ork-20261122-081958-ba4a, item S401: "page up from the last page skips a line at 80x16; 80x24 has only two pages, so the slice tests miss it". The S401 slice tests mostly ran at 80x24, where help has two pages. A paging bug that shows only at a short height, such as the page-up skip, passed `go test ./...` until the UI pass found it by hand at 80x16.

Owner decision adj 570 (`ui.scroll-sweep-home`, Jon, 2026-11-25): the check is a permanent in-tree test in `internal/tui`. It pages down to the end and back up at heights 10, 16, 24 and 40 (width 80) over every scrollable view reachable from `launchHarness`. It fails if any content line never appears. Because it is an ordinary test, `go test ./...` runs it in every slice and in the UI pass (rule u10) with no extra step. The reference content of each view is its own render at a height tall enough to show every line.

Owner decision, 2026-11-25 (adj 570, adj 575): the sweep is a permanent in-tree test. If it finds a real paging defect in an existing view, leave that view or height out of the table with a comment naming a follow-up slice filed with slicer add; S531 lands only the test.

## Failing tests

All in `internal/tui/scroll_sweep_test.go`.

- TestSweepMissingNamesSkippedLines: the pure helper `sweepMissing(want, frames []string) []string` returns the want lines (blank lines ignored) that no frame holds. Given frames that skip one line it returns exactly that line. Given frames that hold every line, including ones that also hold `+N lines above` or `+N more lines` marker lines, it returns nothing. This pins that the sweep can fail.
- TestScrollSweep: a table of scrollable views, each at heights 10, 16, 24 and 40 and width 80. It runs one subtest per view and height. Each subtest sets up the view and sizes the window. It takes the reference lines from the same view at a height tall enough to hold the whole body. It pages down to the end, collecting every frame's lines, then pages back to the top the same way. The sweep fails if either direction's frames miss a reference line, and it names the view, height, direction and line. A sweep that does not reach its end within a frame cap (3 times the reference line count plus 5) also fails. The views are:
  - Help overlay on each of the five tab views, with pgdown and pgup.
  - The Roadmap row list from `launchHarness`, with pgdown and pgup, which move the row cursor and the page window.
  - The launch confirm plan, with down and up, one line at a time. The plan carries enough warnings to exceed the window at height 10.
  - The Roadmap item pane opened on `longItemDetail()`, with pgdown and pgup.

## Implement

1. Create `internal/tui/scroll_sweep_test.go` (SPDX header, `package tui`).
2. Add `sweepMissing(want, frames []string) []string`. It trims each line and drops blank lines and the marker lines `+N lines above` and `+N more lines` from both sides, then returns the want lines no frame holds. Write `TestSweepMissingNamesSkippedLines` first and see it fail before the helper exists.
3. Add `sweepLines(h *harness) []string`: the lines of `plainView(h.m)` with the sidebar column cut at the first `│`, as `helpBody` does, and with the SGR codes already removed by `plainView`. It keeps no screen chrome apart from lines that are the same in every frame.
4. Add `sweepView(t, name, setup func(*harness), pageDown, pageUp tea.KeyPressMsg)`. For each height in `[]int{10, 16, 24, 40}` it runs `t.Run(fmt.Sprintf("%s/h%d", name, height))`, which does the following:
   - build a fresh harness with `setup`, so state never carries between heights;
   - take the reference by sending `tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: 80, Height: 200}` and reading `sweepLines`; the reference is the content no marker hides;
   - resize to `Width: 80, Height: height` and read the first frame;
   - send the page-down key and read each frame until its text stops changing (the end), failing at the frame cap;
   - send the page-up key the same way back to the top;
   - fail when `sweepMissing(reference, frames)` is not empty for the down pass or for the up pass, naming the view, height, direction and the missing lines. Each pass is checked on its own, as `TestHelpPagesCoverEveryLineAtShortHeight` does.
   - Send keys with `tea.KeyPressMsg{Code: tea.KeyPgDown}` and `tea.KeyPgUp` (`press` does not translate these names), and `press("down")` and `press("up")` for the confirm.
5. Add the table in `TestScrollSweep`:
   - Help: for each of `0`, and the waves, roadmap, decisions and questions view constants, set `h.m.view` and press `?`. The setup uses `launchHarness(t)` and sets `h.m.cfg.Live` as it already is.
   - Roadmap list: `launchHarness(t)` on `roadmapView` with no overlay.
   - Launch confirm: `launchHarness(t)` with `l.plan.Warnings` of eight lines, as `TestLaunchConfirmScrollsToClippedWarnings` does, then `launchConfirmed(t, h)`.
   - Item pane: `openLongItemPane(t)`, which swaps in `roadmapLive`.
6. Run `go test ./internal/tui -run 'TestSweepMissing|TestScrollSweep' -v`. If a view fails at some height, that is a real paging defect. Handle it as the owner decides in the Owner needed question below. Do not change views or goldens otherwise.
7. Run `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l .`. Add no changelog entry, because the slice changes no user-visible behaviour.
